notes: The November 2026 BofA Global FMS WAS published Tue 2026-11-17 (fielded Nov 6-12); found on the first query and corroborated across Fortune, Reuters (Yahoo relay), macenews (TradingView relay), vltcapital substack (French), polandinsight, biggo, longbridge x3, kucoin, univest. Headline: tech net overweight collapsed to 12% from 37%, the largest one-month cut since June 2006; 'AI bubble' (34%, from 23%) retook #1 tail risk with 'AI hyperscaler credit event' #2 at 31% (from 11%) while 'disorderly rise in bond yields' fell from 31% to 13% (fourth); 52% now expect a hyperscaler capex cut within six months (from 30%) and a record net 38% say companies are overinvesting, only 16% want more capex (lowest since May 2020); cash fell to 3.6% (from 3.9%, lowest since Aug, cash rule still on sell); equities net 41% OW (from 44%); bonds net 23% UW (from 36/37%), least UW since Nov 2025; growth expectations net 14% weaker (from 4%), inflation expectations net 32% lower (from 5%); soft landing (50%) overtook no-landing (42%), hard landing 3% (from 6%); semis still most crowded at 39% (from 45%) with 'short China stocks' 14% new at #2; Bull & Bear 7.4 (from 8.1) now below the 8.0 sell line (vltcapital only). Hartnett framing (Fortune/biggo): 'end of boom & AI euphoria' / 'the AI boom and euphoria are over', 'pause AI capex' vibe, but not enough fear/capitulation to buy; tactically risk-off. Source disagreements: participants 169/$461bn (Reuters, biggo, hedgefundtips, longbridge) vs 193/$526bn (macenews, Innes substack) - same split as October; bonds prior-month UW 36% (vltcapital) vs 37% (macenews/polandinsight); Oct switch-yield summarised 5.9% vs Nov average 5.8% (vltcapital only, no bucket distribution); B&B 7.4 and switch yield are single-source (vltcapital). Fed hike/cut expectations question not printed in any relay. No Atrani Capital or investinglive Nov-2026 write-up had surfaced at run time; cryptobriefing, mlq failed to fetch (client_error); thedarksideoftheboom paywalled; hedgefundtips charts are images; CNBC refused host.

items.name: BofA Global FMS Nov 2026 - average cash level (% of AUM)
items.source: macenews (TradingView relay) 2026-11-17; Fortune 2026-11-17; Yahoo (Reuters relay) 2026-11-17; vltcapital substack 2026-11-17
items.note: Survey fielded Nov 6-12 2026, published Tue 2026-11-17 (Reuters relay 11:33Z; Fortune 16:07Z; macenews 'released Tuesday'). Participants: 169 managing $461bn (Reuters/Yahoo, biggo, hedgefundtips, longbridge) vs 193 panelists managing $526bn (macenews, thedarksideoftheboom) - same total-panel vs Global-FMS split as October. Cash 3.6% from 3.9% in Oct and Sep (Aug low 3.5%); lowest since August. Cash allocation net 9% underweight (Oct: equal weight) per macenews. BofA cash rule remains on sell signal (<=4.0%) per vltcapital. Corroborated by Fortune ('uber-low 3.6%'), longbridge/Zhitong, biggo, kucoin, polandinsight.

items.name: BofA Global FMS Nov 2026 - most crowded trade
items.note: 'Long global semiconductors' 39% (Oct 45%; Jul record 82%); 'Short China stocks' 14% (new to top-3, first time in at least six months per HKEJ/longbridge); 'Long Magnificent 7' 12% (Oct 16%). 'Short Treasuries' (Oct 27%) dropped out of the top-3.

items.name: BofA Global FMS Nov 2026 - share naming 'long global semiconductors' most crowded
items.note: Down from 45% in Oct, 53% Sep, 82% record Jul 2026. All sources agree on 39%.

items.name: BofA Global FMS Nov 2026 - top tail risk
items.source: macenews (TradingView relay) 2026-11-17; vltcapital 2026-11-17; polandinsight 2026-11-18; Yahoo (Reuters relay) 2026-11-17
items.note: 'AI bubble' 34% (Oct 23%) back to #1; 'AI hyperscaler credit event' 31% (Oct 11%) #2; '2nd wave of inflation' 14% (Oct 20%); 'Disorderly rise in bond yields' 13% (Oct 31%, was #1) fell to fourth. Reuters/Yahoo: inflation and bond-yield concerns 'receded'.

items.name: BofA Global FMS Nov 2026 - share naming 'AI bubble' top tail risk
items.note: Up from 23% in Oct (then #2). Hyperscaler credit event second at 31% (from 11%). Sources agree.

items.name: BofA Global FMS Nov 2026 - net overweight technology
items.source: Yahoo (Reuters relay) 2026-11-17; Fortune 2026-11-17; vltcapital 2026-11-17; polandinsight 2026-11-18; biggo 2026-11-18
items.note: Net 12% OW from 37% in Oct: 25pt drop, largest one-month fall since June 2006 (Reuters: 'by the most in a month since June 2006'). vltcapital: ~0.5 sd below long-term average. Fortune/BofA: best tech entry points historically came when investors cut tech to underweight; November's cut left it overweight. Sector rotation (vltcapital): health care OW 34% from 23% (largest position); discretionary UW 20% from 34%; staples UW 18% from 32%; energy UW 12% from 4%; industrials 19% OW, banks 12% OW; net 71% favour high-quality earnings.

items.name: BofA Global FMS Nov 2026 - net overweight global equities
items.note: Net 41% OW from 44% Oct and 49% Sep. US equities net 13% OW (Oct 11%); EM net 28% OW (Oct 34%); Japan neutral (Oct 9% OW); Eurozone net 5% UW (Oct 8% UW); UK net 21% UW; commodities net 15% OW (Oct 21%); real estate net 23% UW. Bonds net 23% UW (Oct 37% per macenews/polandinsight, 36% per vltcapital), least underweight since Nov 2025.

items.name: BofA Global FMS Nov 2026 - net expecting stronger global growth next 12m
items.note: macenews: 'a net 14% of investors looked for weaker economic growth in the coming 12 months' (Oct net 4% weaker; Sep net 8% stronger); vltcapital: most pessimistic since April. Inflation: net 32% expect lower global inflation in 12m (Oct net 5%; Sep net 4%) - macenews, longbridge/Jin10, vltcapital, polandinsight. vltcapital: 41% expect boom (from 47%), 47% describe outlook as stagflationary.

items.name: BofA Global FMS Nov 2026 - share expecting hard landing / recession
items.unit: pct of respondents expecting hard landing
items.note: Hard landing 3% (Oct 6%); soft landing 50% overtook no-landing 42% (Oct 50%) for the first time since June (vltcapital). Fortune/Reuters/longbridge phrase it as 'only 3% predict a recession' (kucoin: '3% see a 2027 recession').

items.name: BofA Bull & Bear Indicator at Nov 2026 FMS
items.source: vltcapital substack 2026-11-17 (B&B value); Fortune 2026-11-17 (Hartnett wording); biggo 2026-11-18
items.note: Single-source number (vltcapital substack, French): 7.4 'neutral', down from 8.1 in Oct - below the 8.0 sell threshold (buy threshold 2.0). Cash rule still on sell (3.6% <= 4.0%). Broadest FMS sentiment indicator 6.3 from 6.4. Hartnett team (Fortune paraphrase): 'end of boom & AI euphoria' but not enough investor 'fear' / capitulation to buy; tactically risk-off; 'pause AI capex' vibe. biggo: Hartnett wrote 'the AI boom and euphoria are over', recommends defensive allocation.

items.name: BofA Global FMS Nov 2026 - 10y UST yield that would prompt stocks-to-bonds shift
items.note: Single source (vltcapital): average 5.8% (Oct summarised 5.9%); 16% say current levels already suffice (Oct 19%). No distribution by bucket printed this month. Year-end-2027 targets (macenews, vltcapital): 10y UST 4.9% (from 5.1%), EURUSD 1.12, S&P 500 7,926 (from 7,562), gold $4,341. Fed hike/cut expectations question: not printed in any relay found.

items.name: BofA Global FMS Nov 2026 - share expecting an AI hyperscaler capex cut within 6 months
items.source: Fortune 2026-11-17; Yahoo (Reuters relay) 2026-11-17; vltcapital 2026-11-17; longbridge/HKEJ 2026-11-18; kucoin 2026-11-17
items.note: 52% expect at least one AI hyperscaler to announce a capex cut within six months, up from 30% in Oct (Oct: 57% expected no cut). Record net 38% say companies are overinvesting (survey record); only 16% want companies to increase capex, lowest since May 2020. BofA (Reuters relay): the 'big message' is a 'pause or slowdown in AI capital expenditure'. Fortune context: consensus (FactSet) still sees hyperscaler capex +58% next year to ~$1.4tn.

items.name: BofA Global FMS Nov 2026 - likeliest source of a systemic credit event
items.note: 'AI hyperscaler bonds' 38% (Oct 39% named hyperscaler capex) ahead of private credit 30%. Separately 'AI hyperscaler credit event' is the #2 tail risk at 31% (Oct 11%). 2027 best asset class: international equities 36%, US stocks 24%, gold 17%; best index Nasdaq and MSCI EM 21% each, Euro Stoxx 19%; best currency yen 42%, dollar 16%.
